problem_found: 5 of 12 releases are not Friday openers (F01, F02, F10 Thursday; F07 Wednesday; F08 Sunday), so a calendar Fri-Sun window is not comparable across the cohort.
action_taken: Standardized the outcome to opening 3-day India net: Fri-Sun for 11 films, Sun-Tue (Days 1-3) for F08; added is_non_friday_release.
justification: Keeps the studio decision metric (first three days of ticket sales) on one footing while preserving the full 12-film sample.

problem_found: F08 Sikandar released on Sunday 2025-03-30, so it has no Friday or Saturday shows in its opening window.
action_taken: Included F08 with a Sun-Tue (Days 1-3) window and flagged it is_non_friday_release=True for Phase 3 sensitivity testing.
justification: Dropping a 200 crore release would shrink an already small sample and bias the cohort toward Friday openers.

problem_found: F01 Dhurandhar: The Revenge and F05 Dhurandhar are the same franchise, so 2 of 12 rows are not statistically independent.
action_taken: Retained both rows; flagged the overlap for a Phase 3 leave-one-out sensitivity check.
justification: Both are theatrically significant releases, but franchise spillover must be disclosed rather than silently pooled.

problem_found: YouTube commentThreads API returns author PII (authorDisplayName, authorProfileImageUrl, authorChannelUrl, authorChannelId).
action_taken: Stripped all four author PII fields in memory upon ingestion before writing raw JSON or clean CSV.
justification: Project privacy rule prohibits storing or publishing usernames or profile links from review/comment data.

problem_found: order=relevance caps around ~1,200 threads per video (~14,463 total), below the 50,000-row PySpark floor; unioning with order=time can introduce overlapping comment_id rows and embedded CR/LF newlines.
action_taken: Unioned order=relevance and order=time streams per film, deduplicated on comment_id, and normalized CR/LF newlines to spaces.
justification: Clears 50,000+ unique YouTube comments across the 12 trailers while guaranteeing one row per unique comment_id.

problem_found: Same film appears with year suffixes, channel names, and trailer tags across Wikipedia, TMDb, Sacnilk, and YouTube titles.
action_taken: Applied deterministic title normalization (lowercase, stripped years, channel names, trailer noise, punctuation) and verified with rapidfuzz.
justification: Guarantees 12/12 lossless cross-source joins on film_id without silent string-matching mismatches.

problem_found: Cohort spans a 86x budget range (5.5 Cr Su From So to 475.0 Cr Toxic) and 14x trailer view range (7.17M to 101.97M).
action_taken: Computed Min-Max (0-1) and Z-score normalised columns for views, comments, first-7d comments, 3-day India net, and budget.
justification: Puts films of vastly different scale on one footing for cross-metric charts and regression/correlation analysis.

problem_found: YouTube API order=time + order=relevance cap (~5,700 fetched per film) under-samples first-7d counts on mega-trailers with 52K-96K total comments.
action_taken: Computed est_true_first_7d_comments = api_total_comments * (sampled_first_7d_comments / sampled_total_comments) alongside raw counts.
justification: Allows explicit sensitivity testing between raw sampled 7-day counts and scale-adjusted trailer-week comment volume.
